variants.stem: Angles are measured in radians, and a full revolution is 2π radians.

parts.prompt: Convert 390° to radians.
Convert π/3 radians to degrees.
A circle has radius 8 centimeters. Find the length of the arc subtended by a central angle of 270°.

solution: 270° = 3π/2 radians. The arc length is s = rθ = 8(3π/2) = 12π centimeters.

variants.stem: Angles in standard position that share a terminal ray differ by an integer number of revolutions.

parts.prompt: Find the angle with measure from 0 to 2π that has the same terminal ray as 14π/3.
Find the angle with measure from 0 to 2π that has the same terminal ray as −5π/6.
Find the angle with measure from −2π to 0 that has the same terminal ray as 5π/3.

solution: Subtract 2 revolutions, which is 2(2π) = 4π: 14π/3 − 4π = 2π/3.
Add one revolution, which is 2π: −5π/6 + 2π = 7π/6.
Subtract one revolution: 5π/3 − 2π = −π/3.

variants.stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point P(−24, −7).

stimulusBlocks.caption: The terminal ray of θ through P(−24, −7)
stimulusBlocks.alt: A ray from the origin to the point (−24, −7).

parts.prompt: Find sin θ.
Find cos θ.
Find tan θ.

solution: The distance from the origin to P is √((−24)² + (−7)²) = √625 = 25. The sine is the y-coordinate over this distance: sin θ = −7/25.
tan θ is the slope of the terminal ray: −7/−24 = 7/24. It also equals sin θ / cos θ.

variants.stem: Give each value exactly, without a calculator.

parts.prompt: Find sin(2π/3).
Find cos(4π/3).
Find tan(7π/4).

solution: The terminal ray of 2π/3 meets the unit circle at (−1/2, √3/2). The sine is the y-coordinate, so sin(2π/3) = √3/2.
The terminal ray of 4π/3 meets the unit circle at (−1/2, −√3/2). The cosine is the x-coordinate, so cos(4π/3) = −1/2.
The terminal ray of 7π/4 meets the unit circle at (√2/2, −√2/2). So tan(7π/4) = sin/cos = (−√2/2)/(√2/2) = −1.

variants.stem: Give each value exactly, without a calculator.

parts.prompt: Find sin(11π/6).
Find cos(−5π/6).
Find tan(π/6).

solution: The terminal ray of 11π/6 meets the unit circle at (√3/2, −1/2). The sine is the y-coordinate, so sin(11π/6) = −1/2.
The terminal ray of −5π/6, which is also the terminal ray of 7π/6, meets the unit circle at (−√3/2, −1/2). The cosine is the x-coordinate, so cos(−5π/6) = −√3/2.
The terminal ray of π/6 meets the unit circle at (√3/2, 1/2). So tan(π/6) = sin/cos = (1/2)/(√3/2) = √3/3.
